ai.title: Restrict thinkdeeply to explicit planning requests
ai.summary: Updated system prompts in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, `backend/src/planning.ts`, and `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to restrict `think_deeply` usage. The tool is now only invoked when the user explicitly asks for a plan, removing triggers for general complex changes or immediate implementation. `planning.ts` logic simplified to always generate a markdown plan file, removing the option to implement directly. This change affects backend prompt generation logic only.

eli5.text: The assistant behind your service now only thinks through a plan when you directly ask it to make one, rather than whenever your request sounds complicated. It also always saves that plan to a file for you to review before any work begins, instead of sometimes jumping straight to editing things. If you use this service today, you'll notice the assistant won't auto-plan for multi-step changes unless you specifically request planning, and you'll get a written plan document before implementation starts.

ai.title: Add timeout and fallback for Claude planning
ai.summary: Claude planning requests now wrap `promptClaude` with `withTimeout`, enforcing a 4-minute limit in max-cost mode or 100 seconds otherwise. If the timeout triggers, the system logs an error and retries the request without extended thinking enabled. The `withTimeout` utility is added to `common/src/util/promise.ts` to handle promise races and cleanup.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant to plan a complex task, it now sets a generous time limit, four minutes if you're using the highest-power mode, or about 100 seconds otherwise. If the planning step runs past that limit, the assistant saves what it has learned and tries again with a simpler reasoning process turned off, so you still get a plan instead of hanging forever. You won't notice anything different unless planning was about to stall, in which case you'll eventually get an answer rather than no answer at all.

ai.title: Fix search/replace regex for large files
ai.summary: Refined `blockRegex` in `backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts` to allow optional newlines before `>>>>>>> REPLACE` markers, preventing parse failures on large files. Switched retry logic from `promptOpenAI` (o3mini) to `promptClaude` (sonnet) in `backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts`. Exported `handleLargeFile` in `backend/src/process-file-block.ts` and added `response` to logging metadata. Added matplotlib and swe-bench-docker submodules to `evals/test-repos/` for regression testing.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to edit a large file, it now uses a more powerful model that produces search-and-replace edits more reliably. Previously, edits on big files could fail to parse and produce broken results; now those edits apply correctly. The change also records an extra detail (the assistant's full reply) in internal logs when this large-file path is used, so engineers can debug failures more easily. This is live today for large-file edits, and you would notice fewer failed or partial edits on big files.

ai.title: Add ctags to gitignore
ai.summary: Added `tags` to `.gitignore`. Prevents accidental commits of ctags index files. Repo hygiene.

eli5.text: Developers working on this project's code no longer need to worry about accidentally saving a helper file that the computer creates automatically. This helper file, which helps developers navigate the code, is now set to be ignored by the project's tracking system, so it won't clutter the main codebase. The change lives in a behind-the-scenes configuration file and only affects people actively building the software. This is now live today.
